question.text: Kuru Debt Fund holds a INR 100 face value bond with 9% semi-annual coupon. The last coupon was paid 90 days ago; next coupon due in 92 days (assume 182-day period). The bond's quoted clean price is INR 98. What is the dirty price (settlement price including accrued interest)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Semi-annual coupon = 9% / 2 × INR 100 = INR 4.50. Accrued interest is the proportional share of the next coupon earned by the seller for the period elapsed since the last coupon: 4.50 × (90 / 182) ≈ 4.50 × 0.4945 = INR 2.225. Dirty (settlement) price = Clean price + Accrued interest = 98.00 + 2.225 ≈ INR 100.23. The Trap: INR 98.00 ignores accrued interest (the common error of using the clean price as the settlement price); INR 100.22 uses 89/182; INR 102.24 mistakenly adds the full coupon (the full 4.50) instead of the accrued portion. Note: The XIX-D workbook's fixed-income valuation discussion is framed in present-value-of-cash-flows / YTM terms and does not specifically describe clean price, dirty price, accrued interest, or settlement-price mechanics. Treat clean/dirty price computation as general fixed-income knowledge applicable when computing NAV/settlement values for debt-fund holdings.
